decision: NIRVANA source is the OSF view-only link printed in arXiv:2604.07344 section 3.5
why: No account or terms needed; no license is stated on the OSF node, so raw data stays out of git
alternative_rejected: Asking authors

decision: Dedup NIRVANA rows on essay + time + op_type, then order by time
why: Essay 69 logs op_index 82-110 twice; the copies number ops differently and the second holds a paste the first lacks; essay 76 repeats its last two rows
alternative_rejected: Keying on op_index would keep 6 misordered rows. Count is 347 under either key

decision: One window per request, including repeats and very short requests
why: Codebook 2.2 rule 1: a new unit starts at each new request. Short ones are flagged, not removed
alternative_rejected: Dropping "Hi" or "thank you" would be a judgment call on eligibility, left to coding

decision: C2 needs a text-changing editor op after the response and before the next request
why: Codebook 2.3. Cursor, selection and copy alone are not uptake evidence; ChatGPT-side pastes are excluded
alternative_rejected: Counting any op would inflate C2

decision: C2 carries linkage: verbatim_this_response, verbatim_ambiguous or temporal_only, using runs of >=30 shared characters in p, i and d_i ops
why: Codebook section 10: a timestamp alone does not prove a later edit came from a response
alternative_rejected: Calling all C2 linked; paste ops only, which missed long i ops and could credit a run also in earlier text. Changed after the critic's review

decision: Ops between request and response are stored as ops_during_wait, never as uptake
why: They precede the response
alternative_rejected: Treating them as next actions

decision: No time limit on the next-action span
why: The codebook sets none; adding one would be tuning. Latency is stored instead
alternative_rejected: 30-second or 2-minute cutoffs

decision: Use allenai/WildChat-1M, the full 837,989 records, pinned revision
why: Ungated, 3.4 GB, scan takes under a minute. WildChat-1M-Full needs manual approval
alternative_rejected: Subsetting was not needed. The toxic records in the Full version are not screened

decision: Written keyword rule screen on user turns is the rerunnable screen
why: Deterministic and auditable, but recall is limited: research text with no keyword is missed
alternative_rejected: LLM only: not rerunnable

decision: Added 2,000-record draw by lowest hash, in addition to the full corpus
why: To compare at the reported scale. The reported draw method was lost, so this is not a replication
alternative_rejected: Comparing only full-corpus rates

decision: Added cached LLM second pass, model claude-sonnet-5-5, tools off, 25 per batch
why: Rule precision was unknown. Results are cached because reruns would differ, so the cache must be kept for rebuilds. Temperature cannot be set through the CLI. The requested model is recorded; the served model was seen only on a one-call test. Run log printed $3.51, not stored elsewhere. Not verified by a human
alternative_rejected: Subagent reading: settings harder to report

decision: Conversations with an email or phone-like number are dropped from included conversations; masked in LLM excerpts
why: Task forbids copying personal details. A regex cannot catch names, so a residual risk stays
alternative_rejected: Masking text in windows would break tracing to raw

decision: WildChat windows need both rule hit and LLM CLEAR/POSSIBLE; sample uses LLM CLEAR with >=2 user turns only
why: Two filters raise likely precision and continuity. They are not independent: the LLM mostly saw rule-selected conversations, so windows are keyword-biased. LLM positives with no rule hit are reported, not windowed
alternative_rejected: Single filter

decision: WildChat participant_id is a hash of hashed_ip, and country, state and header are never copied
why: Used only to limit clusters. An IP cluster is not a verified person
alternative_rejected: Treating each conversation as a person

decision: Sample split 70 NIRVANA + 30 WildChat. The split is the user's to change at C1
why: NIRVANA has the continuity and editor evidence; WildChat has the research domain. Proportions are a judgment, not derived
alternative_rejected: 50/50: WildChat has no C2

decision: One run of up to 3 consecutive windows per student or conversation
why: Keeps transitions while limiting one student's weight. Windows in a run are not independent
alternative_rejected: All windows of heavy users: top 2 students have 50 windows

decision: Two NIRVANA runs reserved to end on a C0 window
why: C0 is rare (7 of 347) and gold must span coverage. This makes C0 slightly over-represented in the sample
alternative_rejected: Pure random: C0 might not appear

decision: Gold takes at most one window per participant and skips requests of <=2 words
why: Blind human time is scarce and independence matters most there
alternative_rejected: Allowing more than one per student

decision: gold.csv holds request, response, cleaned action text (D20) and the required coverage code, with no rule tier, LLM label or linkage flag
why: Must stay unlabeled for blind coding
alternative_rejected: Sharing sample.csv fields

decision: next_actions_text merges adjacent keystrokes, collapses repeated identical copies, hides cursor and selection ops, and cleans NIRVANA log artifacts (stray closing quote, literal backslash-n, merged cells), and drops typed or deleted ops with no text, for reading only
why: Keystroke-level text is unreadable. Full ops stay in windows.jsonl
alternative_rejected: Showing every op

decision: CSV cells starting with = + - @ get a leading apostrophe
why: Stops spreadsheet apps evaluating dataset text. windows.jsonl keeps the raw text
alternative_rejected: No guard

decision: ScholaWrite downloaded only after the user got access, using their local login; split all_sorted checked for fields and labels only
why: Stop condition: account and terms were the user's to accept. Revision pinned; no token stored in project files
alternative_rejected: Viewer API or third-party copies: would sidestep the gate. Label frequencies: would start a baseline

decision: A blank next user turn gives C0, not C1, and a sample run never skips a turn
why: A blank turn is no usable next action under codebook 2.3. Changed after the critic's review; 14 windows moved, none in the sample
alternative_rejected: Next non-blank turn: would skip a response to a blank turn

decision: Malformed row = extra trailing columns, short row, or a cell holding merged row fields
why: Merged rows were undercounted at first. They are flagged, not repaired; the swallowed ops are not recovered
alternative_rejected: Repairing cells by parsing: risky and beyond this bet
